escena: SCENE (art direction pass on a beverage campaign, studio in Bogota, morning, NO faces): THE SUBJECT OF THE PHOTOGRAPH IS THE CORRECTION, NOT THE HAND THAT MADE IT — verify it by these landmarks: a large printed proof of a key visual for an unbranded craft juice — a cold glass bottle with condensation, half-cut fruit and a band of headline space — lies on the RIGHT half of the worktop, the left part of the frame being the bare dark walnut surface fading into shadow, seen at a steep angle so its paper grain and ink-blue halftone rosette are razor sharp; drawn ON TOP of it in thick ORANGE grease pencil are the marks of a creative director's review — a circle around the bottle, an arrow dragging the fruit across, a firm crossing-out on one element, a bracket in the margin. Those ORANGE marks are the SHARPEST, most deliberate, most contrasted thing in the picture and the eye lands on them first. The grease pencil itself lies on the sheet where it was put down; ANY hand is at most a blurred fragment leaving the frame at the far edge, never the subject. Hard window light rakes across the sheet from the right so the waxy ridge of each pencil stroke throws its own tiny shadow and reads as physical material. 100mm macro at f/5.6. Everything is completely unbranded, no readable text anywhere — the marks are marks, not letters; the proof's headline band is blocks of tone, not words. COMPOSITION FOR A WEBSITE MENU (native to its frame): this horizontal photo is shown small, about 440 pixels wide, inside a dropdown panel; so ONE clear subject reads instantly at that size, sits in the RIGHT half, and the left part is calm continuation of the same scene.

lecho.objeto: the out-of-focus near edge of the dark walnut worktop under the sheet
